C-SEC-EXT-GRANT-BOUND.Summary: Bind each extension's incoming rights to the capability set approved at pairing time — store that grant with the credential, enforce it on every route including /stream/*, and make key replacement honest: success only after the new key verifies and the old one is dead.
C-SEC-EXT-GRANT-BOUND.Problem: Owner-provided 2026-11-21 re-audit of the post-#293/#294/#295 state (C-SEC-EDIT-TARGETING, C-SEC-STREAM-SCOPE, C-SEC-PAIR-REBIND all landed); the three findings are not in the archived findings JSON — the code anchors are current. F-001 (rights can grow after pairing): POST /ext/pair stores the freshly minted secret for whatever extension_id the request names, including a disabled or unregistered extension, because the approval-time declared list comes from registry.get_manifest (registry.rs:205-215), which answers only for enabled registrations and degrades to an empty list otherwise (live_server.rs:568-586, 670-681, 716-739); every incoming data route then resolves permission against the CURRENT manifest at request time inside authenticate_incoming (live_server.rs:530-550), and mt_ext_enable mints or keeps a credential while only flipping the enabled flag (mod.rs:92-105) — so an extension enabled after pairing, or re-registered with a grown manifest, gains incoming rights the approval dialog never showed (tests.rs:1384-1404 exercises enable-after-pair; the gallery toggle is its UI entry, extensionGallery/index.vue:177-192). F-002 (stream routes skip capability checks): the /stream/* handlers authenticate through authenticate_stream/validate_bearer (live_server.rs:443-477, 480-514), which proves enabled identity, bearer possession and owner/epoch fencing but consults no capability — /stream/open (live_server.rs:745-770, 802-840) and the patch/close/heartbeat state changes accept any valid paired token, so an extension never granted stream.document streams documents into the live view, where liveViewer renders whatever arrives (liveViewer/index.vue:50-67); tests.rs:1329-1341 pins the stream route as working on identity alone. F-003 (dishonest key replacement): store_secret inserts the new secret into the memory store and returns Ok even when the keychain write or its read-back verification fails (auth.rs:111-135), while get_secret prefers a readable keychain record and validate_token reads through it (auth.rs:162-176) — after a rebind whose keychain write failed, the OLD keychain record keeps validating while /ext/pair has already answered paired:true with the new secret (live_server.rs:596-602, 629-648, 716-739): the pair response claims a replacement that did not happen.
C-SEC-EXT-GRANT-BOUND.Relationship: Lineage: C-SEC-STREAM-SCOPE (#294) introduced the RouteCapability classes (stream.document, context.read, text.edit, text.insert), the per-route manifest gate on /ext/context and /ext/apply and the honest pairing grant description; C-SEC-PAIR-REBIND (#295) added the constant-time prior-secret rebind gate and confined auto-approval to the test harness; C-SEC-EDIT-TARGETING (#293) added the document-binding fence on /ext/apply; C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH added identity/epoch fencing and serialized stream mutations. All landed. This change only moves WHERE the granted set lives — a pairing-time snapshot enforced by every route instead of the live manifest — and adds stream enforcement (F-002) plus honest replace (F-003) on top; capability names, the rebind gate and the binding fence keep their semantics. The three findings ship as one bundle because they share one object: the approved grant — its snapshot (F-001), its enforcement on the one route family still above it (F-002), and the honesty of the operation that replaces it (F-003).

Goals.Goal: The capability set approved at pairing is stored WITH the key at pairing time, and every route — /ext/context, /ext/apply, /ext/text-insert and every /stream/* route — checks the stored grant, not the live manifest. Enabling after pairing requires the stored grant to still cover what the manifest now requests; otherwise enabling is refused into explicit re-approval (a fresh pairing under the unchanged prior-secret rebind gate).
/stream/* routes require the stored stream.document grant at open and on state changes; owner/generation checks unchanged.
A pair/rebind reports success only after verifying the NEW key validates and the OLD key no longer does; a keychain read error is a distinct state that refuses the rebind.

Constraints.Constraint: Exact ObservedWriteScope, enumerated by reading the current tree:
Wire changes are additive where possible: existing request/response fields keep their names and meaning; the stored grant travels beside the credential, not inside existing fields.

C-SEC-STREAM-SCOPE/#294/#295 lineage preserved: the RouteCapability names (stream.document, context.read, text.edit, text.insert), the fixed grant ordering and the pairing dialog's honest description survive; the prior-secret rebind gate keeps its constant-time comparison and refusal semantics; the C-SEC-EDIT-TARGETING binding fence (400 missing / 409 mismatch, zero events on refusal) is unchanged; C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH owner/epoch fencing, the stream_gate lock order and the disable revocation semantics are unchanged. This change only moves where the granted set lives and adds stream enforcement and honest replace.

Security boundaries: no log line, error message or response ever contains secret material; the stored grant holds capability names only; comparisons stay constant time; the loopback-only binding and Bearer model are unchanged.

Repository artifacts stay English and the GRACE surface stays synchronized (module contracts, graph, verification); no version change, release, publication or deploy is authorized by this specification.

NonGoals.NonGoal: New capability names, manifest schema changes, discovery changes or registry/epoch redesign.

Pairing UX redesign beyond what the goals require: the native approval dialog gains no new surface, the gallery stays a toggle plus error surface, and no new trust-reset mechanism beyond the existing disable command.
Outbound paths: mt_ext_invoke, text_ops and the renderer text-op handling stay untouched; liveViewer/index.vue is evidence only and outside the write scope.
Migration of credentials paired before this change (they hold no stored grant and fail closed until re-approval) — recorded as an assumption for owner confirmation, not silently handled.
Per-operation or time-limited credentials; the one-secret-per-extension-id model stays.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Pairing stores the approved incoming capability set with the credential, and the captured set is exactly what the approval dialog presented: the capture reads the registered manifest whether or not the extension is currently enabled — a disabled-but-registered extension is shown and stored with its real declared set, an unregistered one stores the honest empty grant.

After pairing, every incoming route authorizes by the stored grant: a token whose stored grant lacks the route's capability is refused on /ext/context, /ext/apply, /ext/text-insert and /stream/* even when the extension is enabled and its current manifest declares that capability; a stored credential with no approved grant — including one minted without approval through the enable path — authorizes no incoming route. Rights can no longer grow after pairing without a new approval.

Enabling an extension whose current manifest requests incoming capabilities beyond its stored grant is refused with a distinct logged state that the gallery surfaces as a re-approval instruction; enabling within the stored grant succeeds exactly as today; the disable, fresh pair, enable flow keeps working with its current meaning.

A stored stream.document grant streams exactly as today: /stream/open, patch, close and heartbeat keep their owner/generation/epoch pins and response shapes. An extension whose stored grant lacks stream.document is refused at open and on every state change with no session mutation and no live event emission; the existing stream security regressions keep passing in meaning, with the stream-only pin in enabled_extension_passes_only_declared_capability_routes moving from manifest-derived to grant-derived authorization while keeping the same statuses.

A pair or rebind answers paired:true with a secret only after verification through the effective credential path: the new token validates and, when a credential existed before, the previous token no longer does. Keychain write failure, verification mismatch and keychain read error are distinct logged refusal states; none of them reports success, and a refused rebind never leaves the old key displaced while the response claims a working new one.

New regressions for F-001, F-002 and F-003 fail before the fix and pass after it; the C-SEC-STREAM-SCOPE capability matrix, the C-SEC-EDIT-TARGETING binding matrix and the C-SEC-PAIR-REBIND rebind and denial suites still pass unchanged in meaning.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: The F-001/F-002/F-003 regressions fail before the fix and pass after it; the existing C-SEC-STREAM-SCOPE, C-SEC-EDIT-TARGETING and C-SEC-PAIR-REBIND suites pass with only the pinned stream authorization moved to the stored grant; the extensionGallery renderer suite stays green. Before archiving: grace lint --path . --change C-SEC-EXT-GRANT-BOUND --assertions final --run-commands, then grace lint --path . --assertions current and grace status --path . --with modules --json.

Assumptions.Assumption: The pairing dialog is the native rfd dialog inside live_server.rs handle_pair (release builds); extensionGallery/index.vue contains no pairing dialog — the re-audit anchor at extensionGallery/index.vue:177-192 is toggleExtension, the enable path whose error surface must carry the new re-approval state. The drafting brief's "extensionGallery/index.vue pairing dialog + its tests" is read accordingly: the gallery toggle/error surface plus tests/renderer/components/extensionGallery/index.test.js.
"The extensionGallery vitest suite" means the two suites under tests/renderer/components/extensionGallery/ (index.test.js, textOps.test.js), matching the C-SEC-STREAM-SCOPE verification precedent.
Credentials paired before this change hold no stored grant and therefore fail closed on all incoming routes until re-approved; no migration has been requested and none is planned.
